summary: Mesh AP band-steer + DHCP suppression causes VPN (WireGuard) handshake stall during client roaming
synthesis: Summary: Several employees on the SF office mesh network report short (5-20s) VPN stalls when their device transitions between APs or switches bands. The corporate WireGuard-based zero-trust agent fails to re-establish a fully functional tunnel promptly; upper-layer connections stall and some TCP flows reset. Issue appears correlated with mesh band-steering + DHCP lease behavior when the AP suppresses DHCP renewals during fast L2 handover.
impact: Multiple employees are losing access to internal services briefly during office roaming/hotdesk movements. Affects developer productivity (git pushes/timeouts) and internal dashboards for ~5-10% of devices observed in sampling. Not a full outage but disruptive to interactive workflows.
description:
Issue summary:
- Symptom: During roaming or when client is steered between 5GHz and 2.4GHz SSIDs by the mesh controller, the WireGuard tunnel remains in a 'connected' state but user traffic stalls for 5-20s. After stall, traffic resumes without user intervention.
- Observed at: SF office, floor A-corridor, APs: mesh-zone-3 & mesh-zone-4.
- Client platforms: macOS 13/14, Windows 11, Android 12/13.
- Temporary workaround: manual disable/enable of Wi-Fi or force-wireguard-restart on some clients.

Why this is notable: The agent stays 'up' and handshake messages continue intermittently, but route or DNS state on the client is inconsistent which blocks traffic until timers expire or agent resets. This differs from a full tunnel down (no peer).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Join corporate SSID on a device near mesh-zone-3 (5GHz). 2) Walk towards coverage overlap with mesh-zone-4 where controller enforces band-steer to 2.4GHz. 3) Observe short stall in ssh/git/IDE connections. 4) Run tcpdump on client or capture wireguard logs. 5) Repeat with DHCP debug logging enabled on AP controller.
observed_behavior:
- TCP flows show long retransmit bursts then a few successful packets; many sessions reset by client apps.
- WireGuard user-space logs show repeated keepalive packets from client but no immediate rekey/handshake; peer keeps old endpoint for ~8-12s.
- Client DNS resolver cache shows transient inability to resolve internal hostnames until /etc/resolv.conf (or equivalent) rebinds to correct DNS server.
- DHCP logs on controller show 'suppressed renewal' events during handover windows.
expected_behavior: During fast AP transition the zero-trust agent should quickly rebind routes, maintain peer endpoint mapping, and internal DNS should remain reachable without stall longer than normal roaming (<1s).
logs:
Sample client log (macOS) excerpt:
[2026-03-10T09:12:11.123Z] wg-quick[pid]: Sending keepalive to 52.36.91.12:51820
[2026-03-10T09:12:11.130Z] kernel: en0: link state change, BSSID switch
[2026-03-10T09:12:11.140Z] resolver[scutil]: DNS servers updated -> 10.0.5.2 (suppressed)
[2026-03-10T09:12:18.450Z] wg-quick: handshake attempt failed: timeout waiting for response
[2026-03-10T09:12:21.678Z] app/browser: tcp retransmit, 8 retries

Controller DHCP excerpt:
2026-03-10 09:12:11 SLOW_RENEW client=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF suppressed renewal during fast roam to mesh-zone-4
2026-03-10 09:12:20 RENEW_GRANTED client=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF lease=10.0.5.123

WireGuard capture (server side):
10:12:11.123 IP 10.0.5.123.51820 > 52.36.91.12.51820: IP payload (keepalive)
10:12:18.430 IP 10.0.5.123.51820 > 52.36.91.12.51820: UDP, len 60 (retransmit)
investigation_notes:
Actions taken so far:
- Collected pcap from client and server (tcpdump -i en0 'port 51820') and compared timestamps.
- Reproduced with macOS and Surface; both show same pattern.
- Verified mesh controller is configured for aggressive band-steer and has DHCP 'suppress renewals' option enabled to reduce DHCP storm during roam.
- Tested disabling suppression on a staging AP — when suppression disabled, client roam completed with <1s stall.
- Hypothesis: DHCP suppression delays client refresh of DHCP options (DNS and route push), leaving resolver pointed at an AP-local DNS proxy that is momentarily unreachable, while WireGuard keepalives continue but subsequent traffic fails until lease/route state is reconciled.
- Additional hypothesis: AP's client isolation during micro-handoff briefly blocks UDP flows from reaching local gateway, causing WG handshake timeouts and route flaps.
- Slack thread: #it-support with captures: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0FFEE12/p1678470000000
- Related infra PR to change AP DHCP behavior: github.com/redwood/infrastructure/infra-config/pull/1983
- Reproduction notes: increase AP roam aggressiveness and enable DHCP suppression to trigger in ~3/5 attempts.
temporary_workaround:
1) Disable aggressive band-steer on affected APs (mesh controller setting).
2) If user affected, instruct to toggle Wi-Fi or restart zero-trust agent; this rebinds routes.
3) Short-term: reduce DHCP suppression timer on controller for office zones.
Workaround status: controller change rolled to mesh-zone-4 for experiment; preliminary reduction in reports.
next_steps:
- Coordinate with network team to roll a config change that reduces DHCP suppression window in high-roam areas.
- Evaluate firmware patch or controller upgrade that alters client path pinning during handover.
- Add targeted telemetry to zero-trust agent to surface endpoint rebind events and DNS switch events for future triage.
- Create follow-up INT to track rollout of config across sites if experiment successful.
- Notify workspace ops to monitor for collateral increase in DHCP traffic.
comments: Ava Park (reporter) 2026-03-10: Collected 5 captures, all show the same 8-12s stall window. User reports 2-3 incidents/day while hot-desking.
Liam Chen (assignee) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reproducible. Disabled suppression on mesh-zone-4 and stalled reproductions dropped from ~60% to ~10% in 30 trials. Need ops signoff for broader rollout.

Nina Patel (network) 2026-03-12: Controller change proposal: reduce suppression window from 10s to 1s for office zones tagged 'high-roam'. Opens possible DHCP storm; will add rate-limiter. Planning canary of 3 APs.
SRE (2026-03-13): Observed no increase in DHCP requests post-canary. WireGuard server logs show handshake latency drop from median 9.8s -> 0.9s for canary clients.
